429.description: Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded. Back off before retrying.

400.description: Bad Request — invalid event format or missing required field.

404.description: Not Found — unknown agentId or chatId.

429.description: Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded. Back off before retrying.

post.description: Send one event to the chat and receive a streaming JSON array of events in response. Only one send-event request should be in flight per chat at a time — disable user input until the stream completes. The backend will hold the connection open for up to 60 seconds; clients should match this with an AbortController to avoid stalled connections locking the UI. The response stream includes the same user event that the client sent. If the UI already rendered that message optimistically, ignore the streamed copy with the same _id to avoid showing the shopper's message twice.

target.description: Public direct-call target. Do not send undocumented/internal target names.

payload.description: Target-specific free-form payload for ADD_MESSAGE.USER.DIRECT_CALL. AddMessageUserDirectCallEvent.description: User direct-call event for public direct-call targets. Sent for EVERY quick-reply selection (always DIRECT_CALL, never ADD_MESSAGE.USER.TEXT), whether or not the option carries a target/payload; copy any server-provided target/payload back verbatim. Can also be constructed with the documented target-specific payload shapes.

currency.description: Optional product currency. In chat integrations this is commonly null/omitted; format prices with the frontend/customer-supplied valid ISO 4217 fallback currency.

events.description: Welcome/cold-start events to persist for future replay, including the ADD_MESSAGE.ASSISTANT.COLD_START message shown on the blank-slate screen.

PersistColdStartEvent.description: Persists welcome/cold-start events for future replay. Use this event to save the ADD_MESSAGE.ASSISTANT.COLD_START message; sending the cold-start message itself does not store it in conversation history.

AddMessageAssistantColdStartEvent.description: Actual welcome/cold-start message rendered by the UI and replayed later. Sending ADD_MESSAGE.ASSISTANT.COLD_START directly does not persist it in conversation history. To save the welcome state for future replay, send PERSIST_COLD_START with this event in its events payload.

queries.description: Public metadata: exact search queries the assistant ran. Currently meaningful on assistant carousel events and useful for an optional, merchant-configured see-all-results hand-off to a storefront search page (not shown by default).

batchId.description: Groups the events that make up ONE assistant reply. A single reply can arrive as several events - text, then a carousel, then quick replies - and those share a batchId, so a client can render the first part while the rest still streams in. Two different batchIds are two separate replies. Optional: it is absent on events recorded before it existed, and on every user event, so treat a missing value as "no grouping information" and fall back to grouping consecutive events from the same role that arrive close together.

FatalErrorEvent.description: Fatal, user-facing error. Clients should display the fallback message from general-settings (translated.errorMsg) and stop accepting input for the current turn. The event.text contains internal detail and should NOT be shown to end-users.

ErrorEvent.description: Non-fatal warning emitted by the backend (e.g. internal AGENT.ERROR telemetry). Clients must NOT surface these to end-users — they should be ignored in the UI (logging to a debug panel is fine).

AddMessageAssistantNotificationEvent.description: In-place progress update. Render only the `text` field; `toolName` is internal. Each notification REPLACES the previous one (and replaces the initial "Thinking…" placeholder). Do NOT clear the progress indicator when the first content event arrives; keep it visible while messages stream in and clear it only after the request completes and all response events have been received.

InboundEvent.description: One event from the send-event response stream. **Ignore any event whose `type` is not listed here.** The server also emits internal event types that are deliberately excluded from this contract, and further types may be added without that counting as a breaking change. Dispatch on `type` and treat an unrecognised value as a no-op rather than an error; if you generate a client that deserializes strictly on the discriminator, give it a fallback branch instead of letting it throw.
